members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Our primary objective as co-penholder alongside the United States is to maintain the long-standing technical consensus and secure an unamended six-month extension of UNDOF's mandate, preserving the integrity of the 1974 Disengagement Agreement and safeguarding Syrian sovereignty. We anticipate sensitive discussions with our American co-penholder and Western partners regarding the balance of responsibility for ceasefire violations across the Line of Separation, specifically ensuring that Israeli airstrikes and incursions are adequately reflected alongside non-state armed group activities on the Bravo side. Additionally, we expect to resist any extraneous Western proposals aimed at altering established language regarding Syrian authorities or inserting overly prescriptive, politicized conditionality regarding mission posture and reporting.

messages.Algeria: Algeria fully supports the renewal of UNDOF's mandate as a necessary tool to maintain stability in a highly volatile region. However, the Council cannot continue to ignore realities on the ground extensively documented in the Secretary-General's report, in particular the military presence and incursions by Israeli forces in the area of separation. The resolution must clearly uphold the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria and address all violations of the 1974 Disengagement Agreement.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of UNDOF's mandate for an additional six months to ensure stability in the Golan and prevent further escalation across the region. We appreciate the constructive efforts of the co-penholders, the Russian Federation and the United States, in maintaining a balanced and consensual draft text. China reiterates the importance of full respect for the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, and the safety and security of United Nations peacekeepers.
messages.Denmark: Denmark strongly supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of UNDOF for an additional six months and thanks the co-penholders for their constructive joint stewardship of this file. In a volatile regional security environment, UNDOF plays an indispensable role in maintaining stability and upholding the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. We particularly welcome the draft's clear emphasis on the safety, security, and unhindered freedom of movement of peacekeepers, as well as the robust language on peacekeeping performance and the Women, Peace and Security agenda.
messages.France: France thanks the co-penholders, the United States and the Russian Federation, for circulating this balanced draft resolution renewing the mandate of UNDOF for an additional six months. UNDOF plays an indispensable role in maintaining regional stability, preserving the ceasefire, and monitoring the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement in an increasingly fragile security environment. France fully supports the text as drafted and stands ready to vote in favour.
messages.Greece: Greece welcomes the draft resolution circulated by the co-penholders renewing the mandate of UNDOF for an additional six months. We fully support the text as presented, which appropriately balances the need for stability, the safety and security of UN peacekeepers, and the full implementation of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. Greece stands ready to vote in favour of the draft as it stands.
messages.Guyana: Guyana expresses its full support for the draft resolution renewing UNDOF's mandate until 30 June 2026 and thanks the co-penholders, the Russian Federation and the United States, for maintaining consensus on this critical file. Guyana looks forward to the unanimous adoption of the draft as presented.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan thanks the co-penholders, the Russian Federation and the United States, for presenting a balanced text extending UNDOF's mandate. As a committed troop-contributing country, Pakistan attaches the highest importance to the safety, security, and operational effectiveness of United Nations peacekeepers, as well as strict adherence to the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. We fully support the draft resolution as circulated and look forward to its consensus adoption.
messages.Panama: Panama fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of UNDOF for an additional six months. messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of UNDOF for an additional six months. messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of UNDOF for an additional six months. messages.Slovenia: Slovenia fully supports the draft resolution renewing UNDOF's mandate for an additional six months. messages.Somalia: Somalia thanks the co-penholders, the Russian Federation and the United States, for circulating this balanced draft resolution renewing the mandate of UNDOF. messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom fully supports the draft resolution renewing UNDOF's mandate for an additional six months. messages.United States of America: As co-penholder with the Russian Federation, the United States fully supports this draft resolution renewing UNDOF's mandate for an additional six months. before.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation, together with the United States of America, has submitted the draft resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF) for a further period of six months, until 30 June 2026. 

For more than half a century, UNDOF has played an essential stabilizing role in the Golan, serving as a critical mechanism to maintain the ceasefire between Israel and the Syrian Arab Republic and to prevent any dangerous escalation in an already volatile region. The draft text before us maintains the Force's core mandate, underscores the obligation of the parties to scrupulously adhere to the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, and ensures that the peacekeepers have the necessary support, safety, and resources to fulfill their vital mission. 

We thank all delegations for their constructive engagement during the negotiations, and we call on all members of the Security Council to unanimously support this draft resolution.

after.Algeria:
Algeria voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which renews the mandate of the United Nations Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF) for a further period of six months. We reaffirm our steadfast support for UNDOF and its personnel, who continue to carry out their duties under increasingly complex and volatile conditions. We also thank the co-penholders, the Russian Federation and the United States, for their efforts in facilitating the adoption of this text.

UNDOF remains an indispensable instrument for stability in the region and plays a vital role in monitoring the ceasefire and maintaining the separation of forces in accordance with the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. 

At the same time, Algeria reiterates its principled position that the Syrian Golan is occupied Syrian territory. Lasting peace and stability in the Middle East cannot be attained without bringing an end to the Israeli occupation of all occupied Arab lands, in full conformity with relevant Security Council resolutions, particularly resolution 497 (1981), and the principle of the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force.

We express our grave concern over the continuing violations of the 1974 Agreement, most notably the recurring incursions, military presence, and activities conducted by the Israeli occupying forces in the area of separation. Such actions constitute blatant breaches of the Disengagement Agreement, undermine the mission's operational environment, and jeopardize the safety and security of United Nations personnel. The Security Council cannot remain silent or complacent in the face of these violations.

While we supported the extension of UNDOF's mandate to avoid any security vacuum, we must reiterate our call for the Council to ensure that its resolutions fully reflect the realities on the ground and demand strict adherence by the occupying power to its international legal obligations and existing agreements. 

I thank you.
after.United States of America:
The United States welcomes the Council’s unanimous adoption of today’s resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF) for an additional six months. As co-penholder alongside the Russian Federation, we appreciate the Council’s continued united support for this vital mission.

For over five decades, UNDOF has served as an indispensable stabilizing presence between Israel and the Syrian Arab Republic. Amid ongoing regional volatility, the Force’s role in monitoring the ceasefire and preventing unintended escalation remains as critical as ever. 

Today’s resolution reaffirms that both parties must scrupulously abide by the terms of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. There should be no military forces, unauthorized equipment, or military activities in the area of separation other than those of UNDOF. We call on both parties to exercise maximum restraint, fully respect the ceasefire, and make full use of UNDOF’s liaison mechanisms to de-escalate tensions.

Furthermore, we reiterate our call for all parties to ensure the safety, security, and unhindered freedom of movement of UNDOF personnel, and to allow the mission full access to carry out its mandated tasks safely and effectively. The persistent threats posed by unexploded ordnance, explosive remnants of war, and terrorist groups in the region underscore the challenging conditions in which these peacekeepers operate every day. 

In closing, the United States extends its deepest gratitude to the Head of Mission and Force Commander, Major General Anita Asmah, to the civilian and military personnel of UNDOF and Observer Group Golan, and to the troop-contributing countries for their steadfast dedication and service to the cause of peace and stability in the Middle East.

Thank you.
